hypotheses.claim: Combining the unfarness term (hug isolated unvisited cities early) with a mild residual pull toward the closing/anchor node, both normalized per-step by their maxima, reduces tour length versus pure nearest neighbor on Euclidean TSP without any runtime risk, since per-step cost stays O(|U|^2) and vectorized.

next_search_advice.direction: Vectorized dimensionless farness + destination-pull scoring inside select_next_node: score(u) = -d(cur,u)/s1 + w_f * mean_{v in U\{u}} d(u,v)/s1 + w_t * d(dest_anchor,u)/s1, with per-step max-normalization (dimensionless, scale-invariant) and all features computed with pure NumPy mask/index math in O(|U|^2) per step, keeping full construction within a few ms for n<=200 so 500 ms budget is never at risk.
